title: Legal Issues in Counseling
tagline: The law as a frame for safe, ethical practice.
welcome: Law is not the enemy of counseling; it is the frame that keeps it safe. This course teaches you the legal landscape so you can practice confidently.
vignette: A subpoena arrives for a minor client's records. The counselor must know privilege, consent, and procedure, and act within days. Legal knowledge turns a panic into a procedure.
vignette_attr: A records subpoena, drawn from practice
description: A course in the legal dimensions of counseling children and adolescents: confidentiality, privilege, and their limits with minors; consent and assent; mandated reporting law; custody and divorced-family complexities; records and subpoenas; liability and risk management; and working with the legal system.
questions: What must I keep, what must I break, and what must I report?
Who holds consent when parents disagree?
How do I respond to legal process without betraying the child?
importance: Legal errors end careers and harm children
Minors sit inside complex legal relationships
Confident legal knowledge frees clinical presence
misconceptions: that ethics and law are the same, when they differ and must both be navigated
that legal issues are rare, when they are routine in minor practice
figures: who advanced ethics and law integration
outcomes: You will know what protects and what compels disclosure.
You will manage parental rights and the child's assent.
You will report correctly and document defensibly.
You will stay aligned with legal authority.
You will respond to legal process properly.
You will reduce liability through documentation and consultation.
modules: The frame first, then the practice.
The mature minor and its limits
Reporting is a legal and moral act.
Divided families test your legal clarity.
practicum: A risk-management audit of a practice
tips: Document every legal decision and consultation
When served, pause and consult before acting
integration: Legal competence protects every clinical skill you have built.
faith: We render to law what is law's, and to the child what is the child's, with integrity.
closing: May your practice be safe, your records sound, and your children protected by both.
